question: "A man has to cover a distance of 222 km in 14 hours. If he covers two-third of this distance in 3/7 of the time, then what should his speed (in km/hr) be to cover the remaining distance?"
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Remaining **Distance** = 1/3 of 222 km = 74 km.

Remaining **Time** = 4/7 of 14 hours = 8 hours.

Required **Speed** = 74 ÷ 8 = 9.25 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 9.25 km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f903bd3a995e84e9a2ffb6087ae705079be68b7f828e3968b6760a165162f8d3.png] 

**Given:**

Total Distance = 222 km

Total Time = 14 hours

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered = 2/3 × 222 = 148 km

⇒ Remaining Distance = 222 − 148 = 74 km

⇒ Time taken = 3/7 × 14 = 6 hours

⇒ Remaining Time = 14 − 6 = 8 hours

⇒ Required Speed = Remaining Distance ÷ Remaining Time

⇒ Required Speed = 74 ÷ 8 = 9.25 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 9.25 km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Basic Speed Formula

Speed is defined as the distance covered per unit time. Formula: **Speed = Distance ÷ Time**.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. In this case, the overall average speed is 222 ÷ 14 ≈ 15.85 km/hr.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.</p
